case_name: Novartis India Limited v State Of West Bengal And Others
facts: The Judgment was delivered by : S.B.Sinha, J.
Appellant herein is a successor in interest of a company known as Sandoz (India) Limited.
Respondents were appointed as Sales Representatives by the said Santoz (India) Limited.
In October, 1994 respondent Nos.2 to 4 were transferred to Siwan, Karimganj and Farrukabad respectively.
They filed their representations requesting for withdrawal/cancellation of their respective orders of transfer.
The company, however, asked the respondents to report for duties at their respective transferred places.
Reminders were sent by the company to respondent Nos.2 and 4 on 1st April, 1995 while to respondent No.3 on 31st March, 1995.
As the respondents did not join at their transferred places, they were discharged from services by orders dated 15th April, 1995,
issues: Whether back wages should have been directed to be paid in favour of respondent Nos.2 to 4 by the Industrial Tribunal as also by the High Court of Calcutta
petitioner_arguments: That the Tribunal and consequently the High Court committed a serious error in awarding back wages in favour of respondent Nos.2 to 4 herein without taking into consideration the factors relevant therefor.
Respondents 2 to 4 had not discharged the onus placed on them to show that they were not employed elsewhere during the period of 3rd October, 1994 and the date of the award
The Tribunal applied the wrong test in so far as it proceeded on the basis that the order of termination being bad in law, back wages were to be paid automatically.
Learned Single Judge has failed to arrive at a finding as to why the back wages should be granted.
The Division Bench has also not assigned any reason in support of the findings as to why the back wages should be paid.
respondent_arguments: That the back wages are granted in two different situations; i.e. firstly by way of consequential relief; and secondly by way of a compensation in a case where direction to reinstatement is not possible to be given.

Respondent Nos.2 to 4 having served the company for more than 25 years with all sincerity, their transfer to far away places only a few years prior to their dates of superannuation being mala fide, the same was liable to be set aside.
It was impossible for the respondents to get alternative employment at that age, back wages have rightly been granted in their favour.
holding: The termination of their services was held to be illegal as prior to issuance of the orders, no enquiry had been conducted. Back wages, therefore, could have been granted from the date of termination of service.
The appeal is dismissed with costs.
